title: Mitosis architecture audit and rebuild exploration

completion_criteria.text: Foundational audit of the current engine complete across all four domains: two-layer fan-out, durability/resume, cost/latency, pipeline rigidity + fragility
External research verdict delivered on whether the architecture is correct, with disconfirming pass and cited prior art
The child_process runtime-capability question settled empirically (does dynamic import of node:child_process EXECUTE inside a Workflow script, not merely resolve)

Three open architecture decisions resolved by the user: adopt an off-the-shelf durable-execution runtime vs only its state model; default speculation depth given that rework costs tokens not machine time; which work-type pipelines to define first
An approved architecture spec for the rebuild exists, superseding or explicitly scoping the six paused repair-oriented mitosis threads

spine.active_goal: Architecture is SETTLED and the rebuild is AUTHORIZED (0111). Nothing implemented. Remaining: teach the user the complete picture, then execute the six-step landing order fixed by 0112.
spine.next_step: FIRST TASK, before ANY implementation: a CLEAR breakdown of the complete new architecture and scope for MINIMAL domain understanding - define every term, small organized text (headings/lists/tables), NO large paragraphs, complete picture not a summary. Cover 0107 sandbox pinch, 0106's four layers, 0108 state model, 0109 depth, 0110 fix-first, 0111 polling/end-and-relaunch, 0112 robustness, and the six-step landing order. THEN STOP for the user's reply; do not start step 1.
open_risks: Second-system effect is still the primary danger (0106). Mitigation is 0110's narrow fix-first slice with a machine-checkable oracle, NOT more reviewers.
Wall-clock will barely improve (0104); wins are token cost, crash-loss, twinning tax. Expectations were reset this session and must not drift back.
Determinism is a discipline; replay bugs are subtle (0106). Known trap: 0108 requires the prompt-text hash in the journal key.
Regression risk on what the engine got right: fail-closed halting, and built/awaiting/done. 0112 cuts redundancy, never floors.
LEDGER SPLIT defect: 0103-0106 in the session-continuity-continuity-ledger store, 0107-0112 in session-continuity-inline. A read against the wrong store loses half the architecture record.
Six other paused mitosis threads are now UNBLOCKED and need explicit PER-THREAD disposition by the user. Likely superseded, but the user's call, not the agent's.
Write guard holds all .claude/{hooks,rules,lib,workflows} edits for a human, so landing-order step 1 cannot proceed unattended.
Relaunch trigger for end-and-relaunch is UNRESOLVED (0111), the last design gap in 0108. Candidates: the human's merge action, or a cheap scheduled deterministic check. Webhook excluded.
Dirty tree on feat/centralized-pr-creation: modified .drift-state.json, a test, mitosis.js; untracked .bak-pre-promptsfix-* twins and three specs incl. the vindicated run-readiness-repair spec.
out_of_scope: Implementing landing-order step 1 before the user has received AND responded to the architecture breakdown.
Adopting an off-the-shelf durable-execution runtime - closed by 0108.
Global adaptive speculation windows / AIMD - closed by 0109.
Executing the run-readiness-repair spec's 11 MSPs or quiescent-advance M0-M8, pending per-thread disposition.
Dispatching or restarting any target-repo mitosis run.
Editing the current engine, its twins, or its prompts outside the authorized landing order.
